name: AI-Sentinel
purpose: Checks prompts for injection attacks before they reach an LLM, and checks model output for secrets and personal data.

recommended_for_agents.why: This is now the default whenever a semantic layer is configured. Setting it to false makes the gateway fail open: if the semantic layer is down it silently runs on rules alone, which catch about 10% of unseen attacks.
recommended_for_agents.client_rule: No verdict means no. Treat SentinelError and any non-200 as not allowed.
not_enabled_by_default_in: bare docker run of the gateway image

checks.where: retrieved documents and tool results, before the prompt

measured.source: results/latest.json in yurtseveronder-design/sentinel-eval (authoritative, includes every configuration)
measured.unit: fraction of attacks blocked (catch) and of harmless prompts wrongly blocked (false_block)
measured.blind_set_status: spent: it was used to compare models, so it is optimistic for those choices

sealed_60_prompts.status: unseen, private (hash only is public), authored by an AI, not independent

limits: The default setup (rules + keywords) misses most unseen attacks; a pretrained public classifier (ProtectAI or deepset) is opt-in and raises catch rate (73-97% on the blind set, now used up) at the cost of more false blocks (8-12%).
Test sets are small (25-48 prompts per label); one prompt moves a rate by 2-4 points.
Known misses are listed in data/known_gaps.jsonl in sentinel-eval.
Detects text-level injection; it does not sandbox tools, verify identity, or stop a model from misbehaving on its own.
A first line of defence, not a guarantee.
does_not_store: Prompt text is never written to logs or the audit ledger (length and hash only).
